title.zh: 卷285 列傳七十二 王紫绶 袁州佐 黎士宏 多宏安 王𦈡 张孟球
title.en: Volume 285 Biographies 72: Wang Zishou, Yuan Zhouzuo, Li Shihong, Duo Hong An, Wang Xu, Zhang Mengqiu
title.raw: 卷285 列傳七十二 王紫绶 袁州佐 黎士宏 多宏安 王𦈡 张孟球

sentences.zh: 列傳七十二

translations.literal: Biographies 72
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 72

sentences.zh: 王紫綬袁州佐黎士弘多弘安佟國聘王繻田呈瑞張孟球

translations.literal: Wang Zishou, Yuan Zhouzuo, Li Shihong, Duo Hong'an, Tong Guopin, Wang Xu, Tian Chengrui, Zhang Mengqiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zishou, Yuan Zhouzuo, Li Shihong, Duo Hong'an, Tong Guopin, Wang Xu, Tian Chengrui, and Zhang Mengqiu

sentences.zh: 王紫綬，字金章，河南祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Zishou, courtesy name Jinzhang, was a native of Xiangfu in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zishou, whose courtesy name was Jinzhang, came from Xiangfu in Henan.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Shunzhi reign he became a jinshi and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 散館，授編修。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the Hanlin Academy he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After completing his Hanlin training he was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 乞養歸，僑寓蘇門山中，從孫奇逢講學。

translations.literal: He requested leave to nurse his parents and returned home, residing as a guest in the Sumen Mountains and studying under Sun Qifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave to care for his parents and went home, living in the Sumen Mountains as a guest scholar under Sun Qifeng.

sentences.zh: 居十有七年，母歿，服闋，康熙十二年，授江西贛南道副使。

translations.literal: After seventeen years there his mother died; when mourning ended, in the twelfth year of Kangxi he was appointed vice commissioner of the Gannan Circuit in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He remained there seventeen years until his mother's death; after mourning, in the twelfth year of Kangxi he was appointed vice commissioner of the Gannan Circuit in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，贛南總兵劉進寶有謀略，紫綬推誠結納，預籌防禦。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, the Gannan garrison commander Liu Jinbao was a man of strategy; Zishou won him with sincerity and planned defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, Gannan's garrison commander Liu Jinbao proved resourceful; Zishou won his trust and laid plans for defense ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 既而江西降眾屯墾者相繼叛，惟贛南尚未動。

translations.literal: Thereafter surrendered troops farming garrison lands in Jiangxi rebelled one after another, but Gannan had not yet stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon surrendered troops on garrison farms across Jiangxi rebelled in succession, yet Gannan still held firm.

sentences.zh: 紫綬與進寶謀：「閩、粵反已見端，贛南扼其間，應援前朝故事，設巡撫以資鎮攝。」

translations.literal: Zishou said to Jinbao: "Fujian and Guangdong have already shown signs of revolt; Gannan lies between them. Following precedents of earlier dynasties, we should establish a provincial governor to strengthen control."
translations.idiomatic: Zishou urged Jinbao: "Revolt in Fujian and Guangdong is already visible; Gannan stands between them. As in earlier dynasties, we should petition for a provincial governor to tighten control."

sentences.zh: 申疆吏上請，允之。

translations.literal: They reported upward through the frontier officials and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted the proposal through frontier officials, and it was approved.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賊勢益熾，山寇蜂起，鎮兵疲於奔命，乃練鄉勇以輔之，屢殺賊有功。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year rebel strength grew fiercer; mountain bandits swarmed forth and garrison troops were worn out running to and fro, so he trained local militia to support them and repeatedly killed rebels with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the rebels grew stronger and mountain bandits rose everywhere; with garrison troops exhausted, he drilled local militia to aid them and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 十五年，巡撫白色純及進寶先後卒官，參將周球領鎮兵。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the governor Bai Sechun and Jinbao died in office one after another; the deputy commander Zhou Qiu took command of the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Governor Bai Sechun and Jinbao died in succession; Deputy Commander Zhou Qiu assumed command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 三桂將高得捷、韓大任據吉安，餉道絕，屬縣相繼陷。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's generals Gao Dejie and Han Daren held Ji'an; supply routes were cut and subordinate counties fell in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's generals Gao Dejie and Han Daren held Ji'an, cutting supply lines as dependent counties fell one by one.

sentences.zh: 大任屢致書勸降，送偽署巡撫劄，紫綬斬其使。

translations.literal: Han Daren repeatedly wrote urging surrender and sent a forged commission as governor; Zishou executed his messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren wrote repeatedly urging surrender and sent a forged appointment as governor; Zishou beheaded the envoy.

sentences.zh: 球以乏餉為難，紫綬集士商勸輸間架稅，得白金四萬畀球，餉以無缺。

translations.literal: Zhou Qiu cited lack of funds as a difficulty; Zishou gathered merchants and urged payment of a building-frame tax, obtaining forty thousand taels of silver for Zhou Qiu, so provisions were not wanting.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Qiu pleaded shortage of funds, Zishou rallied merchants to pay a building-frame tax, raising forty thousand taels for him so supplies never failed.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍覺羅舒恕率禁旅下廣東，為尚之信將嚴自明所敗，兵退，距贛州三十里。

translations.literal: The Gannan general Jueluo Shushu led imperial guards south into Guangdong and was defeated by Shang Zhixin's general Yan Ziming; the army retreated to within thirty li of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: General Jueluo Shushu led the Banner guards into Guangdong, was beaten by Shang Zhixin's general Yan Ziming, and fell back to within thirty li of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 自明約得捷由吉安會師夾擊。

translations.literal: Ziming agreed with Dejie to join forces from Ji'an in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming arranged with Dejie to unite their armies from Ji'an in a converging strike.

sentences.zh: 紫綬薦降將許盛率所部漳州水兵五百人益師，夜泅江斫賊營，禁旅繼之，擊敗自明。

translations.literal: Zishou recommended the surrendered general Xu Sheng to lead five hundred Zhangzhou marines to reinforce the army; by night they swam the river and raided the rebel camp, the Banner troops following, and defeated Ziming.
translations.idiomatic: Zishou had the defector Xu Sheng bring five hundred Zhangzhou marines; at night they swam the river and struck the rebel camp, the guards following, and routed Ziming.

sentences.zh: 得捷等勢孤，不敢复窺贛。

translations.literal: Dejie and the others were isolated and dared not again threaten Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dejie and his allies, isolated, no longer dared menace Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵出剿土寇，掠村民，紫綬曰：「鄉民脅從，若並以賊論，贛南二府十六縣將無孑遺。」

translations.literal: When garrison troops went out to suppress local bandits they plundered villagers; Zishou said: "Villagers were coerced; if all are treated as bandits, not a soul will remain in Gannan's two prefectures and sixteen counties."
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops raided villagers while hunting bandits; Zishou warned: "These people were coerced—treat them all as rebels and Gannan's two prefectures and sixteen counties will be emptied."

sentences.zh: 戒鎮將毋妄發兵，飭有司招撫，分別留遣，賑濟難民，境內稍安。

translations.literal: He forbade commanders to deploy troops rashly, ordered civil officials to offer amnesty, sorted who should stay or leave, and relieved distressed people, so the region grew somewhat calm.
translations.idiomatic: He barred reckless deployments, ordered officials to offer amnesty, sorted who to retain or send away, and relieved the destitute until the region quieted.

sentences.zh: 乃規复萬安、泰和兩縣。

translations.literal: He then planned to recover Wan'an and Taihe counties.
translations.idiomatic: He next set out to recover Wan'an and Taihe.

sentences.zh: 自螺山間道達墨潭，可登舟，於是南昌道始通，運餉銀十萬至。

translations.literal: By a path through Luoshan he reached Motan where boats could be boarded, so the Nanchang route was opened and one hundred thousand taels of silver in supplies arrived.
translations.idiomatic: A trail through Luoshan reached Motan where boats could embark; the Nanchang route reopened and a hundred thousand taels of supplies arrived.

sentences.zh: 又發附近倉穀贍軍，人心大定。

translations.literal: He also issued grain from nearby granaries to feed the army, and popular sentiment settled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He released grain from nearby stores to feed the troops, and morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 巡撫佟國禎亦自間道至，始知紫綬已擢浙江督糧道參政。

translations.literal: Governor Tong Guozhen also arrived by a secret route and only then learned that Zishou had already been promoted to grain-intendant of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tong Guozhen arrived by a secret path and learned Zishou had already been promoted to Zhejiang grain-intendant.

sentences.zh: 贛南久不通驛報，大學士李霨言於朝曰：「紫綬死守危疆，三年於茲。

translations.literal: Gannan had long been without courier reports; Grand Secretary Li Ji said at court: "Zishou has held this perilous frontier for three years now.
translations.idiomatic: With no courier news from Gannan for years, Grand Secretary Li Ji told the court: "Zishou has held this desperate frontier three years running.

sentences.zh: 為國惜才，援而出之，猶可大用。」

translations.literal: To spare talent for the state, pull him out while we may—he can still be put to great use."
translations.idiomatic: For the state's sake, recall him while he can still serve greatly."

sentences.zh: 故有是擢。

translations.literal: Hence this promotion.
translations.idiomatic: That was why he received the promotion.

sentences.zh: 紫綬聞命泣下。

translations.literal: On hearing the order Zishou wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the order reached him Zishou wept.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上官，察積弊，歎曰：「糧官不可為也！

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he reported to his superiors, inspected accumulated abuses, and sighed: "The grain office cannot be held!
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he took up his post, surveyed entrenched abuses, and sighed: "This grain office is unbearable!

sentences.zh: 漕截減而軍困，白折浮而民困，吾安忍竭東南之澤而漁之？」

translations.literal: Canal deductions shrink while the army suffers; white-grain surcharges float while the people suffer—how can I drain the southeast's bounty to fish it dry?"
translations.idiomatic: Canal cuts leave the army short while surcharges crush the people—how can I exhaust the southeast to profit from it?"

sentences.zh: 一月即引疾去。

translations.literal: After one month he cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 迨開博學鴻詞科，魏象樞以紫綬與湯斌同薦入試。

translations.literal: When the Boxue Hongci examination was opened, Wei Xiangju recommended Zishou together with Tang Bin to sit for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the special erudition examination opened, Wei Xiangju nominated Zishou and Tang Bin to compete.

sentences.zh: 放還。

translations.literal: They were sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Both were sent home.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 袁州佐，字左之，山東濟寧人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhouzuo, courtesy name Zuozhi, was a native of Jining in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhouzuo, courtesy name Zuozhi, came from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，授陝西乾州知州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed prefect of Qianzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he became jinshi and was made prefect of Qianzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 入為工部員外郎，遷郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as an outer-section clerk in the Ministry of Works and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Works as an outer-section clerk and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 有清直聲，胥吏不敢牟利。

translations.literal: He had a reputation for integrity and uprightness; clerks dared not profit at his expense.
translations.idiomatic: Known for integrity, he kept clerks from profiteering.

sentences.zh: 時山陵工巨，經費浩穰，州佐曰：「民困極矣，寸縑尺縷，皆閭閻膏血！」

translations.literal: At the time imperial tomb works were vast and expenses enormous; Zhouzuo said: "The people are at their limit—every inch of silk is blood from their homes!"
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tomb works were vast and costly; Zhouzuo said: "The people are exhausted—every inch of cloth is their lifeblood!"

sentences.zh: 力清乾沒，司焚帛，省金錢鉅萬。

translations.literal: He vigorously cleared embezzlement, supervised burning of sacrificial silks, and saved vast sums.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted out graft, oversaw ritual burning, and saved vast sums.

sentences.zh: 出為陝西甘山道僉事。

translations.literal: He went out as assistant administration commissioner of the Ganshan Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as assistant commissioner of the Ganshan Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 青海蒙古諸部覬得大草灘為牧地。

translations.literal: Mongol tribes of Qinghai coveted the Great Grass Beach as pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Mongol tribes eyed the Great Grass Beach for pasture.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，偕提督張勇度地畫界，堅拒，寢其議。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, together with Provincial Military Commissioner Zhang Yong he surveyed and marked the border, firmly refused them, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9, with Commissioner Zhang Yong he surveyed the border, stood firm, and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 自後青海蒙古諸部人不敢复窺邊。

translations.literal: Thereafter Qinghai Mongols dared not again encroach on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After that Qinghai Mongols no longer raided the border.

sentences.zh: 歲協西寧餽運，負載千里，甘州民苦之，州佐力請得罷。

translations.literal: Each year Xining supplies were delivered by convoy a thousand li; Ganzhou people suffered; Zhouzuo petitioned successfully to end it.
translations.idiomatic: Annual Xining convoys over a thousand li burdened Ganzhou; Zhouzuo had the practice abolished.

sentences.zh: 甘州駐兵數千，待餉急，力為籌備，軍得宿飽。

translations.literal: Several thousand troops were stationed at Ganzhou awaiting pay urgently; he worked hard to provision them so the army ate its fill nightly.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of troops at Ganzhou needed pay; he provisioned them so they ate full every night.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷直隸口北道參議。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to assistant intendant of the Koubei Circuit in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became assistant intendant of Koubei in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 地確民貧，逋課積累，倉儲歷歲侵漁，耗蝕無算。

translations.literal: The land was barren and the people poor; tax arrears piled up and granaries had been plundered year after year with incalculable loss.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was poor, taxes in arrears, granaries plundered yearly beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 州佐請按籍覈實，清宿蠹。

translations.literal: Zhouzuo requested verification against the registers to clear long-standing corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzuo asked to verify registers and purge old corruption.

sentences.zh: 大吏懼以失察得罪，陽韙而陰沮之。

translations.literal: Superiors feared conviction for negligence; they praised him openly while obstructing him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors feared negligence charges; they praised him to his face while blocking him behind his back.

sentences.zh: 州佐擘畫盤錯，致疾乞休，未去官，卒。

translations.literal: Zhouzuo wrestled with tangled affairs, fell ill and begged retirement, and died before leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Wrestling with knotty affairs he fell ill, sought retirement, and died still in post.

sentences.zh: 州佐在甘州久，言邊境要害戰守狀，原委斠然。

translations.literal: Having long served at Ganzhou, he spoke of frontier strongpoints, war, and defense with clear mastery of detail.
translations.idiomatic: Long at Ganzhou, he spoke of frontier defense with exhaustive clarity.

sentences.zh: 謂邊地民稀，宜用開中法，分河東鹽引三之一輸粟河西資軍食；

translations.literal: He said the borderlands were sparsely peopled and the kaizhong method should be used, allotting one third of Hedong salt licenses to deliver grain west of the river for army food;
translations.idiomatic: He urged the kaizhong salt trade: one third of Hedong salt quotas could feed armies west of the river;

sentences.zh: 又宜簡練鄉勇，拔置卒伍，不待召募，可坐收精銳。

translations.literal: local militia should also be drilled and selected into the ranks so elite troops could be gathered without waiting for recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: militia should be drilled and drafted so elite troops need not wait on recruitment.

sentences.zh: 時詔簡監司具才望者入為卿貳，州佐在選，會卒，未及用。

translations.literal: An edict then selected outstanding circuit intendants for ministry posts; Zhouzuo was on the list but died before appointment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict chose distinguished circuit officials for central posts; Zhouzuo was selected but died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 黎士弘，字媿曾，福建長汀人。

translations.literal: Li Shihong, courtesy name Kuiceng, was a native of Changting in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shihong, courtesy name Kuiceng, came from Changting in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少讀書山中二十年，篤於孝友。

translations.literal: In youth he read in the mountains twenty years, devoted to filial piety and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied in the mountains twenty years, steeped in filial piety and fraternity.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，舉順天鄉試，授江西廣信府推官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was appointed reviewing officer of Guangxin prefecture in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he passed the Shuntian provincial exam and became reviewing officer of Guangxin in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 鋤強糾貪，姦宄斂戢。

translations.literal: He uprooted the powerful and corrected corruption; villains shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: He uprooted bullies and punished graft until wrongdoers quailed.

sentences.zh: 理讞牘，脫無罪數百人，時為語曰：「遇黎則生。」

translations.literal: Handling cases he freed hundreds of innocents; people said: "Meet Li and you live."
translations.idiomatic: In trials he freed hundreds of innocents; people said, "Meet Li and you live."

sentences.zh: 署玉山縣事。

translations.literal: He served concurrently as magistrate of Yushan county.
translations.idiomatic: He also acted as magistrate of Yushan.

sentences.zh: 兵后城中草三尺，不辨街巷，居民才三十二家。

translations.literal: After the wars grass in the city stood three feet high, streets indistinguishable, and only thirty-two households remained.
translations.idiomatic: After war grass stood three feet high in the streets; only thirty-two households remained.

sentences.zh: 士弘立學建治，招集流亡，墾田定賦，民復舊業。

translations.literal: Shihong established schools and government, gathered refugees, opened fields and fixed taxes, and people resumed their old livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools and offices, gathered refugees, opened fields and set taxes, and people returned to their trades.

sentences.zh: 裁缺，改授永新知縣。

translations.literal: When the post was abolished he was reassigned magistrate of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: When the post was cut he became magistrate of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 政清獄簡，與民休息。

translations.literal: Government was clear and prisons light; he let the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was clean, prisons sparse, and the people rested.

sentences.zh: 舊例，二月開徵，五月解其半。

translations.literal: By old custom collection opened in the second month and half was remitted in the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: By custom tax collection opened in the second month and half was due in the fifth.

sentences.zh: 士弘陳於上官曰：「縣小民窮，二月寫租十石，貸銀一兩，三月可減至六石，四月則三石。

translations.literal: Shihong told his superiors: "The county is small and the people poor; in the second month ten piculs of rent written down cost one tael borrowed; by the third month it falls to six piculs, by the fourth to three.
translations.idiomatic: He told superiors: "This small county is poor—in the second month ten piculs on the books cost a tael in loans; by the third month six piculs, by the fourth three.

sentences.zh: 請以四月開徵，五月解，展兩月之徵，已為窮民留數万之糧。」

translations.literal: Please open collection in the fourth month and remit in the fifth; delaying collection two months would leave the poor tens of thousands of piculs of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Open collection in the fourth and remit in the fifth—two months' delay would save the poor tens of thousands of piculs."

sentences.zh: 布政使劉楗素寬仁，即允之。

translations.literal: The provincial treasurer Liu Jian was by nature lenient and granted it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Treasurer Liu Jian, naturally mild, agreed at once.

sentences.zh: 甲訴乙悔婚。

translations.literal: A sued B for breaking a betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: One party sued another for breaking a betrothal.

sentences.zh: 鄉俗婚書各裝為卷，書男女生辰。

translations.literal: Local custom bound marriage documents separately as scrolls recording the birth dates of bride and groom.
translations.idiomatic: Locally each marriage contract was a scroll with the couple's birth dates.

sentences.zh: 兩造固鄰舊，女生辰所素悉，偽為卷為證。

translations.literal: The parties were old neighbors; the girl's birth date was well known, so a forged scroll was made as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: As neighbors the girl's birth date was known; a forged scroll was produced.

sentences.zh: 士弘先問媒證：「乙得甲聘禮若干？

translations.literal: Shihong first asked the matchmaker: "How much betrothal gift did B receive from A?
translations.idiomatic: Shihong first asked the matchmaker: "How much betrothal gift did B take from A?

sentences.zh: 行聘時有何客？」

translations.literal: Who were the guests at the betrothal?"
translations.idiomatic: Who attended the betrothal?"

sentences.zh: 媒證出不意，妄舉以對。

translations.literal: Caught off guard, the matchmaker answered at random.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard, the matchmaker invented answers.

sentences.zh: 復問甲，所對各異。

translations.literal: Asked again of A, the answers differed.
translations.idiomatic: Questioning A, the answers did not match.

sentences.zh: 擘視捲軸，竹猶青，笑詰之曰：「若訂婚三載，捲軸竹色猶新，此非臨訟偽造者乎？」

translations.literal: Splitting the scroll he saw the bamboo still green and laughed: "If you were betrothed three years, would the bamboo still be fresh? Is this not forged for the lawsuit?"
translations.idiomatic: He split the scroll—the bamboo was still green—and laughed: "Betrothed three years and the bamboo is fresh? This was forged for court."

sentences.zh: 甲乃服罪。

translations.literal: A then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The plaintiff then confessed.

sentences.zh: 縣吏左梅伯有叔富而無子，梅伯糾賊劫殺之，獲賊而梅伯逃。

translations.literal: The clerk Zuo Meibo had a wealthy childless uncle; Meibo incited bandits to rob and kill him, the bandits were caught but Meibo fled.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zuo Meibo's uncle was rich and childless; Meibo hired bandits to kill him; the bandits were caught but Meibo escaped.

sentences.zh: 士弘抵任，叔妻哭訴，陰跡梅伯匿安福勢宦家，故緩詞曰：「此舊事。

translations.literal: When Shihong took office the uncle's wife wept and appealed; he secretly traced Meibo hiding with a powerful family in Anfu, so he spoke mildly: "This is an old case.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office the widow appealed; he traced Meibo to a powerful Anfu household and said mildly, "This is an old affair.

sentences.zh: 前官不了，余安能按之？」

translations.literal: My predecessor could not finish it—how can I pursue it?"
translations.idiomatic: My predecessor left it unsettled—how can I take it up?"

sentences.zh: 數月，梅伯歸，叔妻复訴，置不問。

translations.literal: Months later Meibo returned; the widow appealed again and he ignored it.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Meibo returned; she appealed again and he ignored it.

sentences.zh: 梅伯且出收叔遺產，叔妻號於庭曰：「公號廉明，今寬殺人者罪，且佔寡婦田，何得為廉明！」

translations.literal: Meibo went out to seize the uncle's estate; the widow wailed in court: "You are called incorrupt—now you spare a murderer and seize a widow's land—how is that incorrupt!"
translations.idiomatic: Meibo seized the estate; the widow cried in court: "They call you upright, yet you spare a killer and take a widow's fields—what uprightness is this!"

sentences.zh: 陽怒，批其牘曰：「止問田土，不問人命。」

translations.literal: Feigning anger he wrote on her petition: "I inquire only about the land, not the killing."
translations.idiomatic: Feigning anger he wrote: "I ask only about the land, not the killing."

sentences.zh: 梅伯益自得，赴縣訴理，乃笑謂曰：「候汝三載矣！」

translations.literal: Meibo grew bolder and came to sue; Shihong smiled: "I have waited for you three years!"
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened, Meibo sued; Shihong smiled: "I have waited three years for you!"

sentences.zh: 批其牘曰：「止問人命，不問田土。」

translations.literal: He wrote on the petition: "I ask only about the killing, not the land."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "I ask only about the killing, not the land."

sentences.zh: 梅伯遂伏法。

translations.literal: Meibo was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Meibo was executed.

sentences.zh: 其善斷獄多類此。

translations.literal: His skill in judging cases was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his judgments were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 考最，擢陝西甘州同知。

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he was promoted to subprefect of Ganzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Rated top, he was promoted subprefect of Ganzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 复考最，擢江南常州知府。

translations.literal: Rated highest again, he was promoted prefect of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Rated top again, he became prefect of Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂亂起，關隴震動，大吏疏請擢洮西道副使，未到官而洮、岷陷。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui's rebellion broke out the northwest shook; superiors memorialized to promote him to vice commissioner of the Taoxi Circuit, but before he took office Tao and Min fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rebelled the northwest shook; he was nominated vice commissioner of Taoxi, but Tao and Min fell before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 邊外群番乘亂內犯，肆剽掠，調署甘山道。

translations.literal: Tribal groups beyond the border raided inward in the chaos; he was transferred to act as Ganshan commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Border tribes raided in the turmoil; he was posted to act as Ganshan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 王輔臣叛，河東失守。

translations.literal: Wang Fuchen rebelled and Hedong was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen rebelled and the east bank of the river was lost.

sentences.zh: 士弘以兵集當謀帥，言於巡撫，謂：「恢復河東，非用河西兵不可；

translations.literal: Shihong, seeing troops gathered, said a commander was needed and told the governor: "To recover Hedong, Hexi troops must be used;
translations.idiomatic: With troops massed he told the governor: "Recovering Hedong requires Hexi troops;

sentences.zh: 用河西兵，非責之提督張勇不可。」

translations.literal: to use Hexi troops, Commissioner Zhang Yong must be charged with it."
translations.idiomatic: and Hexi troops require Commissioner Zhang Yong."

sentences.zh: 疏入，授勇靖逆將軍，節制諸鎮。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; Yong was made Pacification General and given command of all garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent; Yong became Pacification General commanding all forces.

sentences.zh: 复蘭州，士弘贊畫功為多。

translations.literal: Lanzhou was recovered; Shihong's planning merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou was retaken; Shihong's planning counted most.

sentences.zh: 署甘肅按察使，按失守官吏罪，務平允。

translations.literal: Acting as provincial judicial commissioner of Gansu, he tried officials who lost their posts, striving for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Gansu judicial commissioner, he tried officials for lost posts with scrupulous fairness.

sentences.zh: 寧夏兵叛，殺提督陳福，調寧夏道。

translations.literal: Ningxia troops rebelled and killed Provincial Military Commissioner Chen Fu; he was transferred to the Ningxia Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningxia troops mutinied and killed Commissioner Chen Fu, he was posted to the Ningxia Circuit.

sentences.zh: 嚴守禦，安反側，免衛所逋糧七萬五千石。

translations.literal: He defended strictly, settled unrest, and remitted seventy-five thousand piculs of grain arrears from guard posts.
translations.idiomatic: He held the defenses, quieted unrest, and waived seventy-five thousand piculs of guard-post grain arrears.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，寇平，以功進布政使參議。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the rebels were pacified; for merit he was promoted to administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16, with the rebels subdued, he was promoted administration commissioner for his service.

sentences.zh: 母老乞歸，家居幾三十年。

translations.literal: His mother was old; he begged to return and lived at home nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: His mother aged; he sought retirement and lived at home nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 士弘備兵甘山時，取晉辛憲英語：「軍旅之間可以濟者，惟仁與恕。」

translations.literal: When Shihong was preparing troops on the Ganshan frontier he took a saying of the Jin dynast Jin Xianying: "In military affairs what can help is only benevolence and forbearance."
translations.idiomatic: While readying troops on Ganshan he quoted Jin Xianying: "In camp only benevolence and forbearance avail."

sentences.zh: 因以名其堂。

translations.literal: He therefore named his hall for it.
translations.idiomatic: He named his hall accordingly.

sentences.zh: 多弘安，字君修，直隸阜城人。

translations.literal: Duo Hong'an, courtesy name Junxiu, was a native of Fucheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Hong'an, courtesy name Junxiu, came from Fucheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，選拔貢生。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi he was selected as a tribute student by special promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 he was chosen as a specially promoted tribute student.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授廣東靈山知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Lingshan in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi he became magistrate of Lingshan in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 兵後荒殘，居無衙舍。

translations.literal: After the wars the land lay waste and he had no yamen to live in.
translations.idiomatic: After war the district was ruined and he lacked even a yamen.

sentences.zh: 弘安請免積年逋賦，招撫流移，捐給牛種，民得安耕稼。

translations.literal: Hong'an requested exemption of years of tax arrears, gathered refugees, and donated oxen and seed so the people could farm in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an secured remission of tax arrears, gathered refugees, and gave oxen and seed until farming resumed.

sentences.zh: 葺城垣，創學宮，繕官廨，捕除盜賊，靈山大治，士民刊石紀其績。

translations.literal: He repaired walls, founded a school, rebuilt offices, and captured bandits; Lingshan was greatly ordered and gentry and people carved stone to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt walls, founded a school, repaired offices, and suppressed bandits; order returned and the people set up a stone memorial.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷奉天承德知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred magistrate of Chengde in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became magistrate of Chengde in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 旗、民抗法者，送部懲治，皆懾服。

translations.literal: Bannermen and civilians who resisted the law were sent to the ministry for punishment and all submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Law-breaking Bannermen and civilians were sent to the ministry for punishment and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢陝西延安靖邊同知。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted subprefect of Jingbian in Yan'an, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made subprefect of Jingbian in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 十六年，補江南淮安山盱河務同知。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed subprefect of the Shan'ou River works at Huai'an in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became subprefect of Shan'ou River works at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 時高堰長堤潰決，淮水注寶應、高郵，不復出清口敵黃。

translations.literal: At the time the Gaoyan long embankment burst; Huai River water poured into Baoying and Gaoyou and no longer met the Yellow River at Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyan embankment burst; Huai water flooded Baoying and Gaoyou and no longer met the Yellow River at Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 黃水直注里河，運道淤淺，复隨淮入堰，無由會清口下云梯關入海，近海口盡淤墊。

translations.literal: Yellow water poured straight into the inner river; the transport channel silted shallow, then followed the Huai into the embankment with no way to meet Qingkou and descend Yuntiling to the sea; near the estuary all was silted up.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River water filled the inner channel; transport routes silted, then the Huai backed into the embankment with no outlet to Qingkou and the sea—the estuary choked with silt.

sentences.zh: 弘安與河督靳輔籌策築高堰，束淮敵黃，治爛泥淺諸故道，導清水入里河，運道乃通。

translations.literal: Hong'an with River Director Jin Fu planned to build Gaoyan, confine the Huai against the Yellow River, dredge the Lanni shallow and other old channels, and guide clear water into the inner river so the transport route opened.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an with Director Jin Fu built Gaoyan to pin the Huai against the Yellow River, dredged old channels, and sent clear water into the inner river until transport reopened.

sentences.zh: 修築兩岸及河口清江大閘，與淮工相表裡。

translations.literal: He repaired both banks and the Qingjiang sluice at the river mouth, complementing Huai River works.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired both banks and the Qingjiang sluice at the mouth, matching the Huai works.

sentences.zh: 清河達雲梯關數百里，葭葦榛蕪，壅塞故道。

translations.literal: The cleared river to Yuntiling stretched hundreds of li through reeds and brush choking the old channel.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of li to Yuntiling were choked with reeds blocking the old channel.

sentences.zh: 用以水攻沙法，塞周橋、高澗諸閘，使清淮無旁洩，蓄全力攻積沙。

translations.literal: Using the method of attacking sand with water, he blocked the Zhouqiao and Gaojian sluices so clear Huai water would not leak aside and stored full force to scour accumulated sand.
translations.idiomatic: By "using water to fight sand" he closed Zhouqiao and Gaojian sluices, kept Huai water from leaking off, and concentrated force to scour silt.

sentences.zh: 十七年，大雨，淮盛漲，與黃併入海。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year great rain fell; the Huai swelled and together with the Yellow River entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year heavy rains swelled the Huai, which entered the sea with the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 治淮、治黃、治運，並收成效。

translations.literal: Control of the Huai, Yellow River, and transport all achieved results together.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, Yellow River, and transport control all succeeded together.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢淮安知府。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted prefect of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became prefect of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢淮揚道。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted Huai-Yang intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he became Huai-Yang intendant.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，擢安徽按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted Anhui provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became Anhui judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時方議浚下河、治高堰。

translations.literal: At the time debate was underway on dredging the lower river and repairing Gaoyan.
translations.idiomatic: Debate was underway on dredging the lower river and repairing Gaoyan.

sentences.zh: 弘安入覲，疏陳：「高堰宜急治，無論下河開浚與否。

translations.literal: Hong'an on audience memorialized: "Gaoyan should be repaired urgently, regardless of whether the lower river is dredged.
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an at audience memorialized: "Gaoyan must be repaired at once, whether or not the lower river is dredged.

sentences.zh: 治堰法，砌石先安地釘，湖底水深，費帑甚繁。

translations.literal: For embankment work, laying stone must first set ground nails; the lake bottom is deep and treasury expense very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Stone facing needs ground nails first; deep lake bed makes costs enormous.

sentences.zh: 如用板若掃，水勢盪掣，尤易摧殘。

translations.literal: If boards or fascines are used, surging water will batter them and destruction comes easily.
translations.idiomatic: Boards or fascines are easily destroyed by surging water.

sentences.zh: 惟密釘排椿，內實以碎石，庶可敵風浪，省金錢。

translations.literal: Only densely nailed row piles packed with broken stone can withstand wind and waves and save money.
translations.idiomatic: Dense row piles packed with rubble resist wind and waves and save funds.

sentences.zh: 十餘年後，黃河刷深，則湖、河水俱卑，高堰既固，下河亦漸就理。」

translations.literal: After ten-odd years the Yellow River will scour deeper and lake and river water both lower; once Gaoyan is firm the lower river will gradually be set right."
translations.idiomatic: In ten years the Yellow River will scour deeper, waters will fall, Gaoyan will hold, and the lower river will right itself."

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷江西布政使，乞歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred Jiangxi administration commissioner and begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Jiangxi administration commissioner and retired.

sentences.zh: 後值黃、運兩河潰溢，起用弘安。

translations.literal: Later when the Yellow and transport rivers burst and overflowed, Hong'an was recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow and transport rivers burst again he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 會病卒，祀靈山名宦。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died before taking office; he was enshrined in the Lingshan temple of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness before reporting; Lingshan enshrined him among eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 佟國聘，字君莘，奉天人。

translations.literal: Tong Guopin, courtesy name Junxin, was a native of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guopin, courtesy name Junxin, came from Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 以廕生補吏部筆帖式。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was made a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he became a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，授江南碭山知縣，縣當黃河衝，研求治河方略。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi he was appointed magistrate of Dangshan in Jiangnan; the county lay in the Yellow River's path and he studied river-control strategy deeply.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 he became magistrate of Dangshan on the Yellow River and studied control strategy deeply.

sentences.zh: 擢歸仁堤同知，調宿桃同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted subprefect of the Guiren embankment and transferred subprefect of Sutao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Guiren embankment subprefect, then Sutao subprefect.

sentences.zh: 擢貴州平遠知府，河督靳輔疏留任，十餘年倚如左右手。

translations.literal: He was promoted prefect of Pingyuan in Guizhou; River Director Jin Fu memorialized to keep him—more than ten years he was relied on like a right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Pingyuan prefect in Guizhou, Jin Fu kept him—over ten years as his right hand.

sentences.zh: 塞楊家莊、蕭家渡決口，建硃家堂、溫家廟二石壩，浚白洋引河九道，築黃河南、北兩岸堤，浚中河，靡役不從。

translations.literal: He closed breaches at Yangjiazhuang and Xiaojiadu, built stone dams at Zhujiatang and Wenjiamiao, dredged nine channels of the Baiyang diversion, built embankments on north and south banks of the Yellow River, and dredged the middle river—no task he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He closed Yangjiazhuang and Xiaojiadu breaches, built Zhujiatang and Wenjiamiao stone dams, dredged nine Baiyang channels, built north and south embankments, and dredged the middle river.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢山東濟寧道副使。

translations.literal: After long service he was promoted vice commissioner of the Jining Circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted vice commissioner of Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道地為漕運樞紐，卹夫役，減苛稅，除冗費，能舉其職。

translations.literal: The circuit was the hub of grain transport; he comforted corvée labor, reduced harsh taxes, and cut redundant expenses, able to fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: As hub of grain transport he eased corvée, cut harsh taxes and waste, and fulfilled his post.

sentences.zh: 復調監督高堰工程。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to supervise Gaoyan works.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to supervise Gaoyan works.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 王繻，字慎夫，河南睢州人。

translations.literal: Wang Xu, courtesy name Shenfu, was a native of Suizhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu, courtesy name Shenfu, came from Suizhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少學於湯斌。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Tang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十五年，以歲貢生授直隸東明知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi, as a senior tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25, as senior tribute student, he became magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 糧賦多欺隱，易甲長，大戶使族長督之，飛灑不行，流亡來歸。

translations.literal: Grain levies had much concealed fraud; he changed the headmen so great households had clan heads supervise them—false registration ceased and refugees returned.
translations.idiomatic: Grain fraud was rampant; he replaced headmen so clan elders supervised great households—false rolls ended and refugees returned.

sentences.zh: 民間養官馬為累，力除之。

translations.literal: The people were burdened raising official horses; he abolished it resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the burden of raising official horses.

sentences.zh: 撫盜魁，責以緝捕，盜絕跡。

translations.literal: He pacified bandit chiefs and charged them with capture duty; bandits vanished.
translations.idiomatic: He won over bandit chiefs and charged them to hunt bandits until none remained.

sentences.zh: 逃人誣攀良民，雪之。

translations.literal: Fugitives falsely implicated innocent people; he cleared them.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives had framed innocents; he exonerated them.

sentences.zh: 民有繼妻素淫，欲並亂前妻女，不從，戕之死。

translations.literal: A man had a stepmother who was wanton and wished also to violate his daughter by the first wife; she refused and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: A stepmother tried to violate her stepdaughter; the girl refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 繻謂母道絕，當故殺妻前夫子律論斬，報可，因著為例。

translations.literal: Xu said the mother's way was severed and she should be sentenced to decapitation under the statute for killing a stepson's child; approval was granted and it became a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Xu held the mother's bond severed and sought decapitation under the statute for killing a stepson's child; the court approved and made it precedent.

sentences.zh: 母憂去，服闋，補獲鹿。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office; after mourning he was reassigned to Huolu.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death and mourning he was posted to Huolu.

sentences.zh: 治驛有法，民不累於供億。

translations.literal: He managed courier stations effectively so the people were not worn down by supply duties.
translations.idiomatic: He ran courier stations well so supply duties did not burden the people.

sentences.zh: 內遷戶部員外郎，擢郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as an outer-section clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Revenue as clerk and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，出為江南糧儲道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he went out as grain-intendant of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he became Jiangnan grain-intendant.

sentences.zh: 道舊有倉規銀鉅萬，繻一擯勿取。

translations.literal: The circuit had warehouse customary silver of tens of thousands of taels; Xu rejected it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The post carried tens of thousands of taels in customary fees; Xu refused them all.

sentences.zh: 將徵漕，扁舟行縣，懲其濫收者。

translations.literal: Before collecting grain transport he went by small boat through the counties and punished those who collected excessively.
translations.idiomatic: Before grain collection he toured counties by skiff and punished excessive levies.

sentences.zh: 至宜興，宜興民曰：「吾民四十年不見糧道，今飛來耶？」

translations.literal: At Yixing the people said: "Our people have not seen a grain intendant in forty years—has one flown here?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yixing people said: "Forty years without a grain intendant—has one flown here?"

sentences.zh: 號曰「飛糧道」。

translations.literal: They called him the "Flying Grain Intendant."
translations.idiomatic: They nicknamed him the Flying Grain Intendant.

sentences.zh: 道庫歲收銀八十五萬兩，為修船及弁丁運費。

translations.literal: The circuit treasury collected eight hundred fifty thousand taels yearly for ship repair and transport clerks' expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury took 850,000 taels yearly for ships and transport staff.

sentences.zh: 運丁預支行糧，例扣月息，丁益困，繻悉罷之。

translations.literal: Transport laborers received grain advances with monthly interest deducted by custom, increasing their hardship; Xu abolished it all.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers' grain advances carried monthly interest; Xu abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted Jiangsu provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he became Jiangsu judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 治獄仁恕，多所平反。

translations.literal: In judging cases he was benevolent and forgiving and reversed many verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: He judged with mercy and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 宿州生攜妻子出客授，妻兄女來視，居數日，妻子併中毒死，妻兄素有隙，疑其女置毒，告官，被刑誣服。

translations.literal: A Suzhou student took wife and children to teach elsewhere; his wife's brother's daughter came to visit and after several days wife and children all died of poison; the brother had old enmity and was suspected; he was tortured into confession.
translations.idiomatic: A Suzhou teacher's family was poisoned; his wife's brother was suspected and tortured into confessing.

sentences.zh: 繻疑之，問其室來往復何人，得十二歲學徒畏師嚴置鏚食中狀，事乃白。

translations.literal: Xu doubted it, asked who came and went in the house, and obtained a twelve-year-old pupil's account that fearing the teacher's severity he had put arsenic in the food—the truth came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xu doubted, asked visitors, and learned a twelve-year-old pupil had poisoned the food from fear of harsh teaching—the truth emerged.

sentences.zh: 無錫民毆攻皮匠，匠死，僧與民仇，證為鬥毆殺。

translations.literal: A Wuxi man beat a tanner who died; a monk who hated the man testified it was killing in brawl.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuxi a man beat a tanner who died; an enemy monk claimed brawl killing.

sentences.zh: 繻察鬥毆日月在保辜限外，詰曰：「傷重何不醫？」

translations.literal: Xu saw the brawl date fell outside the period of grace for wounds and demanded: "If the injury was severe why was there no medical care?"
translations.idiomatic: The brawl fell outside the grace period for wounds; Xu asked why there was no medical care.

sentences.zh: 出醫方，則匠死於傷寒，僧乃服。

translations.literal: The prescription was produced and the tanner had died of cold—the monk then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The prescription showed death from cold—the monk confessed.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，入覲，顧宋犖曰：「朕聞繻督糧時官聲甚好。」

translations.literal: On the emperor's southern tour Xu had audience; the emperor said to Song Luo: "I hear Xu's reputation as grain intendant was very good."
translations.idiomatic: On the southern tour the emperor told Song Luo: "I hear Xu was an excellent grain intendant."

sentences.zh: 時繻已病，遣御醫視之，賜德里雅噶藥一器，溫旨慰諭，复賜御書。

translations.literal: Xu was already ill; an imperial physician was sent, a vessel of delijiagao medicine bestowed, warm words of comfort, and imperial calligraphy again given.
translations.idiomatic: Already ill, he received an imperial physician, delijiagao medicine, warm words, and imperial calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 繻曰：「按察任大責重，臥治即辜恩。」

translations.literal: Xu said: "The judicial commissioner's responsibility is great; to govern from bed would betray grace."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said: "A judicial commissioner's burden is heavy—ruling from bed would betray the emperor's grace."

sentences.zh: 引疾歸，年甫五十。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned, aged only fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on illness at only fifty.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After long time he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home years later.

sentences.zh: 田呈瑞，字介璞，山西汾陽人。

translations.literal: Tian Chengrui, courtesy name Jiepu, was a native of Fenyang in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengrui, courtesy name Jiepu, came from Fenyang in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，仕為中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era he served as a Secretariat draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he served as Secretariat draftsman.

sentences.zh: 出襄南河事。

translations.literal: He went out to manage south Henan river affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to manage south Henan river works.

sentences.zh: 有堤當水沖，曰：「此堤一壞，萬家其魚矣！

translations.literal: There was an embankment in the water's direct rush; he said: "If this embankment breaks, ten thousand households will be fish!
translations.idiomatic: An embankment faced the main current; he said: "If it breaks, ten thousand homes become fish in the flood!

sentences.zh: 土堤易修易敗，宜更以石。」

translations.literal: Earthen embankments are easy to repair and easy to fail; stone should replace them."
translations.idiomatic: Earth works fail easily—stone should replace them."

sentences.zh: 家素豐，出私錢成之。

translations.literal: His family was wealthy; he spent private funds to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: His family was wealthy and he paid from private funds.

sentences.zh: 以功擢大名道，未之任，調陝西臨洮道。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted Daming intendant but before taking office was transferred to Lintao Circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Daming intendant for merit, he was transferred to Lintao before taking office.

sentences.zh: 遇飢治賑，策馬行郡縣山谷間，豪右胥吏不敢為奸弊。

translations.literal: Meeting famine he organized relief, riding through prefectures and mountain valleys so powerful families and clerks dared not commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he rode through counties and valleys organizing relief so bullies and clerks dared not cheat.

sentences.zh: 呈瑞念救荒無善策，於蘭州西石佛灣鑿渠，教民造水車，引以溉田，歲增粟十餘萬石，民為建生祠。

translations.literal: Chengrui thought there was no good policy for famine relief; at Shifowan west of Lanzhou he cut a canal, taught people to build water wheels, and irrigate fields—increasing grain more than a hundred thousand piculs yearly; the people built a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He cut a canal at Shifowan, taught water wheels, and added over a hundred thousand piculs yearly; the people built a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 調浙江金衢嚴道，署糧儲道，徵漕積弊盡洗滌之。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Jinqu-Yan Circuit in Zhejiang, acting as grain-intendant, he washed away all accumulated abuses in grain transport collection.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang grain-intendant acting he purged transport abuses.

sentences.zh: 值旱，冒暑省荒，感疾，乞歸不得。

translations.literal: In drought he braved heat inspecting famine and fell ill; he begged to return but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In drought he inspected famine in heat, fell ill, and was denied retirement.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 張孟球，字夔石，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mengqiu, courtesy name Kuishi, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengqiu, courtesy name Kuishi, came from Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十四年進士，授山東昌樂知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Changle in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 24 he became jinshi and magistrate of Changle in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 入為工部主事。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Works as secretary.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出督雲南學政，父​​憂去，服闋，補福建糧驛道。

translations.literal: He went out as educational commissioner of Yunnan; when his father died he left; after mourning he was reassigned grain-courier of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Yunnan educational commissioner; after his father's death and mourning he became Fujian grain-courier.

sentences.zh: 駐防軍食取給於漕。

translations.literal: Garrison troops' food came from grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison rations came from the transport system.

sentences.zh: 上游四郡阻灘險。

translations.literal: The four upper prefectures were blocked by shoals and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Four upstream prefectures faced dangerous shoals.

sentences.zh: 故事，徵解折色，官為採置，輒抑勒病商。

translations.literal: By precedent collection was in commuted silver and officials procured goods, always squeezing merchants.
translations.idiomatic: By custom tax was commuted to silver and officials procured goods, squeezing merchants.

sentences.zh: 孟球於延、建產米地平價購米，僦民船運省城，不假吏胥，諸弊盡絕。

translations.literal: Mengqiu bought rice cheaply in Yan and Jian where land was level, hired civilian boats to the provincial capital, used no clerks, and all abuses ended.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu bought rice cheaply in Yan and Jian, hired civilian boats to the capital without clerks, and abuses ended.

sentences.zh: 地多山嶺，官吏濫用驛夫，孟球禁革私冒。

translations.literal: The land had many mountains; officials abused courier laborers; Mengqiu forbade private misuse.
translations.idiomatic: In mountainous country officials abused couriers; Mengqiu forbade private impressment.

sentences.zh: 遇大徭，預期發僱值，終其任無擾驛者。

translations.literal: When major corvée came he issued hire wages in advance; throughout his term no courier stations were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: For major corvée he paid hire wages upfront, and courier stations were never harassed during his term.

sentences.zh: 調河南糧儲道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grain-intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted grain-intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河南漕糧，就衛輝水次收兌。

translations.literal: Henan transport grain was received and exchanged at the Weihui river landing.
translations.idiomatic: Henan grain transport was collected and exchanged at the Weihui river landing.

sentences.zh: 舊無倉廒，又無額役，運船調之他省。

translations.literal: Formerly there were no granaries and no quota labor; transport boats were reassigned from other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: There had been no granaries or quota labor; transport boats were drawn from other provinces.

sentences.zh: 天寒水涸，糧不時至，宿河干以待，遇雨雪則米濕霉變，又患盜竊。

translations.literal: In cold weather when water dried up grain did not arrive in time; it waited on the dry riverbed, and in rain or snow the rice grew damp and moldy, with theft also feared.
translations.idiomatic: When winter dried the rivers, grain piled on the banks, spoiled in rain and snow, and was stolen.

sentences.zh: 孟球始以羨餘建倉。

translations.literal: Mengqiu first used surplus funds to build granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu first used surplus revenue to build granaries.

sentences.zh: 署布政使。

translations.literal: He acted as administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 西藏用兵，調河南馬騾萬，凡騾馬三需一夫，剋期兩月。

translations.literal: Troops were used in Tibet; ten thousand horses and mules were levied from Henan—every three pack animals required one laborer, with a deadline of two months.
translations.idiomatic: For the Tibet campaign Henan supplied ten thousand horses and mules—three animals per laborer, due in two months.

sentences.zh: 孟球止宿郊外，躬自檢閱，西路近陝諸郡遣吏往督之，盡除需索留難諸弊。

translations.literal: Mengqiu lodged outside the city and personally inspected; for western routes near Shaanxi he sent officials from nearby prefectures to supervise, eliminating all abuses of demands and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu camped outside the city and inspected personally; on western routes near Shaanxi he sent officials to supervise and ended extortion and delays.

sentences.zh: 凡五十四日，馬驢如數遣赴軍，而民不擾。

translations.literal: In fifty-four days horses and mules were dispatched to the army in full numbers while the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In fifty-four days the full quota reached the army without troubling the people.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蘭陽民硃復業附白蓮教，自稱明裔，煽惑數縣。

translations.literal: A Lanyang commoner Zhu Fuye joined the White Lotus teaching, called himself a Ming descendant, and incited several counties.
translations.idiomatic: A Lanyang man, Zhu Fuye, joined the White Lotus sect, claimed Ming descent, and stirred several counties.

sentences.zh: 孟球檄杞縣知縣寧君佐馳往捕治，盡獲其黨。

translations.literal: Mengqiu ordered the Qi county magistrate Ning Junzuo to ride swiftly to arrest and punish them, capturing the whole party.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu ordered Qi magistrate Ning Junzuo to ride out and capture the entire sect.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書張廷樞往按，從孟球議，誅其與逆謀者，愚民被誘悉釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister Zhang Tinglu to investigate; following Mengqiu's proposal those who joined the rebellion were executed and deluded commoners who were enticed were all released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister Zhang Tinglu to investigate; following Mengqiu, conspirators were executed and duped commoners released.

sentences.zh: 淅川營兵博，知縣崔錫執而罪之，兵譁，執南陽知府沈淵，眾辱之，總兵高成不能治。

translations.literal: Xichuan garrison soldiers gambled; Magistrate Cui Xi arrested and punished them; the soldiers mutinied, seized Nanyang Prefect Shen Yuan, publicly humiliated him, and Regional Commander Gao Cheng could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Xichuan garrison soldiers gambled; Magistrate Cui Xi punished them; they mutinied, seized Prefect Shen Yuan of Nanyang and humiliated him, and Commander Gao Cheng could not restore order.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫張聖佐坐譴，孟球護巡撫，曰：「南陽地連襄、鄖，急則鋌而走險，事未可知。」

translations.literal: At the time Governor Zhang Shengzuo was under reprimand; Mengqiu acted as governor and said: "Nanyang borders Xiang and Yun; pressed hard, desperate men will take rash risks—the outcome is uncertain."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Shengzuo was under censure; acting in his place Mengqiu said: "Nanyang borders Xiang and Yun—push too hard and desperate men may turn violent; the outcome is uncertain."

sentences.zh: 密令附近諸縣嚴守禦，諭：「止誅首惡，自首免罪。」

translations.literal: He secretly ordered nearby counties to defend strictly and proclaimed: "Only the ringleaders will be executed; those who surrender will be spared."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered neighboring counties to hold firm and proclaimed: "Only ringleaders die; surrender and you are spared."

sentences.zh: 得倡亂者七人誅之，不數日而事定。

translations.literal: Seven who led the disorder were executed and within days the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Seven ringleaders were executed and within days order returned.

sentences.zh: 康熙末，乞歸，不復出。

translations.literal: At the end of Kangxi he begged to return and never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kangxi he retired and never served again.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign he died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 論曰：官監司卓卓有名氏，即平進至督撫，易耳。

translations.literal: The critique says: Officials of commissioner and intendant rank who stand out with famous integrity can easily advance by regular steps to governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: distinguished circuit officials can readily rise by routine promotion to governor-general.

sentences.zh: 如紫綬等皆早退，遂以監司終。

translations.literal: Men like Zishou all retired early and thus ended their careers as circuit officials.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zishou retired early and ended as circuit officials.

sentences.zh: 紫綬崎嶇兵間，捍偏隅為民保障；

translations.literal: Zishou struggled through war, holding a remote corner as the people's bulwark;
translations.idiomatic: Zishou held a remote corner through war as the people's shield;

sentences.zh: 州佐、士弘勤勤重民事；

translations.literal: Zhouzuo and Shihong diligently stressed the people's affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhouzuo and Shihong tirelessly served the people's needs;

sentences.zh: 弘安贊治河；

translations.literal: Hong'an assisted in governing rivers;
translations.idiomatic: Hong'an aided river control;

sentences.zh: 繻善斷獄；

translations.literal: Xu excelled at judging cases;
translations.idiomatic: Xu excelled in judging cases;

sentences.zh: 孟球能應變：使得為督撫，其績效當有大於是者。

translations.literal: Mengqiu could adapt to change: had he become governor-general, his achievements would surely have been greater than these.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqiu could meet emergencies: as governor-general his achievements would surely have surpassed these.

sentences.zh: 時方承平，仕得行其意，知止知足，必有說以自處矣。

translations.literal: The age was at peace; officeholders could act on their convictions; knowing when to stop and when to be content, they surely had their reasons for how they conducted themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In a peaceful age they could act on conviction; knowing when to stop and be content, they surely had their reasons.
